ratings_why.fun: Over a 7 because a Guise brings its tribe: a Kit in a Bird's Guise flies south, Pip mirrors a Pass into a second lane, Moll's Stocks keep sold text, and keep-or-swap is a real choice every turn.
ratings_why.distinct: Exchange with the shop and stealing the enemy's text across are new to Bramble, but copying text is a familiar shapeshifter idea from other games.

verdict_why: The v1 loop is closed and nothing left is broken; more passes would mostly make it different, not better.

points.text: Say on The Fetch that the Stock copies the carry's own text, not the Guise it wears; with a Changeling carry, players will expect the borrowed text.
Placement Officer only repeats the Clerk. Let the unit you take arrive wearing the given unit's Guise, so the two verbs feed each other.
Pip Unlike shines only on text with a direction in it. A fallback when the text has none would keep her live in more lobbies.
Keep the off-label tricks (freeze an Exchanged unit as an eighth slot, buy back to replay When played, Moll on an Exchange); they are the tribe's best moments.

standouts.why: Wicker Moll turns every sell or Exchange into a kept text plus fodder for the next Exchange.
Counter Stand-In makes selling a decision: which text do you keep as you let the body go?
The Lady stacks Belly, Mire and Pass on one body, a capstone that is different every game.

weakest.why: Placement Officer is a repeat of the Clerk with no twist of its own.
Veil-Stitcher is a plain End of Turn buffer with a light Guise check.
Bettie Underhill is a counter payoff; it pays but asks for no new play.

flags.note: "Guise" of a Changeling carry could mean its own text or what it wears; the keyword says own text, but the card reads the other way.
Keeper of the Lost Hour with the Lady doubles every borrowed fight trigger on one body; the high roll worth the owner's eye.
Coat-Peg Steward adds +2/+2 per Exchange; with Clerk, Officer and Midnight Swap that is several a turn, plus Bettie's count.
